questions.knowledge_point: Solving a Factored Inequality Involving an Exponential Function and a Polynomial
questions.worked_solution:
When we have an inequality involving an exponential function with a positive base, we're allowed to multiply or divide both sides by the exponential function.

Dividing both sides of the given inequality by $(0.33)^{2x-5},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(4{x}^{6}+3)\cdot (0.33)^{2x-5} & \ge 0 \\ \frac{(4{x}^{6}+3)\cdot (0.33)^{2x-5}}{(0.33)^{2x-5}} & \ge \frac{0}{(0.33)^{2x-5}} \\ 4{x}^{6}+3 & \ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$

Furthermore, $4{x}^{6}+3\ge 0$ for all values of $x.$

Therefore, the solution is all real numbers.

When we have an inequality involving an exponential function with a positive base, we're allowed to multiply or divide both sides by the exponential function.

Dividing both sides of the given inequality by ${2}^{3x},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}({x}^{2}-25)^{3}\cdot {2}^{3x} & <0 \\ \frac{({x}^{2}-25)^{3}\cdot {2}^{3x}}{{2}^{3x}} & <\frac{0}{{2}^{3x}} \\ ({x}^{2}-25)^{3} & <0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve the inequality using familiar methods:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[3]{({x}^{2}-25)^{3}} & <\sqrt[3]{0} \\ {x}^{2}-25 & <0 \\ {x}^{2} & <25 \\ \sqrt{{x}^{2}} & <\sqrt{25} \\ |x| & <5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the inequality is $-5<x<5.$

Dividing both sides of the given inequality by ${6}^{3x-2},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(49-{x}^{2})^{3}\cdot {6}^{3x-2} & \le 0 \\ \frac{(49-{x}^{2})^{3}\cdot {6}^{3x-2}}{{6}^{3x-2}} & \le \frac{0}{{6}^{3x-2}} \\ (49-{x}^{2})^{3} & \le 0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve the inequality using familiar methods:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[3]{(49-{x}^{2})^{3}} & \le \sqrt[3]{0} \\ 49-{x}^{2} & \le 0 \\ -{x}^{2} & \le -49 \\ {x}^{2} & \ge 49 \\ \sqrt{{x}^{2}} & \ge \sqrt{49} \\ |x| & \ge 7\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we had to flip the sign again of the inequality since we divided by a negative number ($-1$).

Therefore, the solution to the inequality is $x\le -7$ or $x\ge 7.$
